The expected root cause centers on a card-testing attack: a specific client (198.51.100.30) performing POST /checkout/payment requests at a high rate around 18:05-18:06 UTC, which is the actual abusive/malicious traffic pattern that matters, with the recommended fix being a new rate-based rule scoped to /checkout/payment (not switching the site-wide rule to Block, since that would also block legitimate automation). The investigation summary completely misses this card-testing attack on /checkout/payment and the attacker IP 198.51.100.30. Instead, it identifies the Artillery load-test traffic (198.51.100.10) hitting GET /catalog as the "abusive" traffic needing to be blocked, and recommends switching the site-wide rate rule from Count to Block as the root-cause fix — which is explicitly the wrong fix according to the expected answer (since that would block the known legitimate automation, not catch the actual card-testing attack). The investigation also fails to mention the sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20. The investigation misidentified the benign automation (Artillery) as the abusive traffic while completely missing the actual malicious traffic pattern (card testing on checkout). This is a fundamentally different and incorrect root cause attribution.</reasoning>
